history.summary: A very large 2260sqft 3BR at $1100 psf — ~24% below the Riversound median of $1455, the deepest PSF discount in the batch. But the $2.486M total price and reliance on Kangkar LRT only (no MRT) make it a niche, slow-moving exit. 6.5%/yr appreciation on 137 txns is good; the question is who buys a $2.5M leasehold OCR unit without an MRT.
history.rating_rationale: The cheap PSF is real but largely an artifact of size: a 2260sqft layout at $2.486M sits above the deepest buyer band ($1.8-2.5M edge) and is served only by Kangkar LRT, which thins the buyer pool versus MRT-fronting peers. For an investment hold, liquidity and yield matter more than headline PSF — and a 2260sqft unit yields poorly per dollar while appealing mainly to a narrow large-family segment. 6.5%/yr CAGR and a well-regarded 590-unit Qingjian development keep it from Avoid, but the size/price/exit profile caps it at Neutral.

history.summary: A 99-LH Sengkang 4BR asking $1,355 psf — below the project's ~$1,406 psf 12-month average on deep data (137 txns), so reasonable value in a favorable OCR region. But $2.0M is near the quantum ceiling for a Sengkang 4BR, capping the buyer pool and exit liquidity.
history.rating_rationale: The value side is decent: asking $1,355 psf is ~4% below Riversound's trailing-12-month average of $1,406 psf (range $1,025-$1,570), backed by 137 transactions — far from a thin-data quirk. D19 is OCR with the most favorable realized forward drift (~+4.0%), and ~84 years of lease remain (least lease-decay risk of the leasehold names here). What holds me at Neutral rather than Buy: (1) the size-cohort premium of -4.2% rests on only 3 cohort txns, so the size-specific 'cheapness' is thin even if the project-level value is solid; (2) the binding constraint is quantum — $2.0M for a compact (1,475 sqft) 4BR sits near the top of what Sengkang resale buyers pay, and HDB-upgrader budgets thin out sharply above this level, so exit liquidity for a 4BR at this price is the real risk; (3) transport is moderate (Buangkok NE15 / Sengkang LRT, not on the doorstep). Trailing 6.5% CAGR (137 txns) is credible but ~0 forward power, so it does not change the call. Net: fairly-to-mildly-cheaply priced asset in a good-region, but the quantum ceiling caps upside and liquidity — an honest Neutral.

history.summary: A genuine 1,475 sqft 4BR in a sound, deeply-traded Sengkang project — but the ask sits 8-12% above every price-adjusted print this oversized format has ever achieved, and it is the project's thinnest-liquidity unit type (3 sales in 14 years).
history.rating_rationale:
The 775 score is inflated by two identifiable artifacts, and the unit's own comps say the ask is too high.

COMP WORK (the crux). MMR reads this as -13.0% cheap vs age-adjusted D19 peers in the 1400-1800 sqft band. That band is the wrong comp: at Riversound, 1400-1800 sqft is not a normal apartment, it is the oversized/dual-key/PES format, and it trades at a structural discount to the project's core stock. Holding FLOOR CONSTANT (all comparisons within floors 01-05), the 1450-1600 sqft format printed 12.1% below core 900-1400 sqft units in 2021, 9.0% below in 2022, and 12.8% below in 2025 - a -9% to -13% format discount replicated across three separate years. Indexing the project's own core-size PSF ($1,078 in 2021 -> $1,455 in 2026) onto the format's three prints puts them at $1,213-$1,263 psf in 2026 money = $1.79M-$1.86M on 1,475 sqft. The ask is $2.00M / $1,356 psf, i.e. +8% to +12% over its own format's adjusted level.

The floor cannot rescue it. Within core sizes the entire floor premium is small: fl 01-05 $1,334 -> fl 16-20 $1,441 psf (+8% bottom to top tier, 2024-26). Applying the format discount to a floor-matched base gives fair value of ~$1.81M (low floor) to ~$1.95M (top tier, 2026 vintage). Even the most generous assumption only reaches the ask - it never beats it.

LIQUIDITY IS THE SECOND STRIKE. The 1450-1600 sqft format has THREE recorded sales in the project's 14-year history (all floors 01-05, 100% low-floor share) against 61 project prints in 24 months alone. This is the type nobody trades. Layer on a $2.0M quantum in Sengkang where realsmart shows 65% of buyers are HDB upgraders - that ceiling thins the exit pool exactly where this unit sits.

SCORE ARTIFACTS. (1) The size-band comp above drives age_value +9.95, the largest single positive MMR component. (2) mrt +4.16 credits '400m to MRT' - but the listing's own field reads '420m from SE4 Kangkar LRT'. This is LRT, not MRT; Buangkok NE15 is not walkable. A known scorer issue that adds roughly +100 score_1000 on Sengkang/Punggol stock.

WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD, and it is not nothing. realsmart REALSCORE 3.9/5 with 99.6% of resales profitable - 275 profitable vs 1 unprofitable across 276 resales, avg holding 7.7 yrs, avg annualized return 4.8%. That is a deep, trustworthy book (well past the 150-resale trust bar) and it is real downside evidence: almost nobody has lost money owning here. Add OCR/D19 (the strongest realized forward-return region), 590 units with a very deep buyer pool, ~85 yrs lease remaining, and a bedroom count that checks out (bed_bands 'ok': 4BR band 1150-1550 sqft on 35 URA rental contracts - not a relabel). But that record was earned by owners entering at $936-$1,174 psf. It does not underwrite a $1,356 psf entry into the format's own premium.

THE ARITHMETIC. A ~10% entry premium plus ~$73k of entry costs is roughly three years of this project's own historical 4.8% annualized return consumed before breakeven - on 2.67% gross / 1.44% net yield, so the carry does not fund the wait. The repo's ROI projections (5.9-6.0% annualized) run off a 6.5% trailing URA CAGR that the backtest says has ~zero forward power, and momentum is already negative (-0.684).

This revises the 2026-06-09 Neutral on this same unit at the same price. That call benchmarked the ask against the project's ~$1,406 psf 12-month average - a size-mix error, since that average is set by 900-1400 sqft stock. Format-controlled, the right comp is ~$1,260 psf, and the verdict moves down.

Confidence is medium, not high: the unit's floor is undisclosed (PropertyGuru optional field, absent here) and would move fair value by ~8%, and the format discount rests on 3 prints. But that thinness is itself the liquidity argument, and the -9/-12/-13% replication across three years is consistent. At ~$1.85M this is a different conversation; at $2.00M it is a pass.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: $4,450/mo estimated from 10 URA project-level 4BR contracts (confidence 0.95) = 2.67% gross, 1.44% net. Weak carry for a $2.0M outlay and correctly penalized by MMR (yield -4.92). If the unit is in fact a 4BR Dual Key (the 1421-1776 sqft type overlapping this size), splitting the keys could lift gross rent somewhat - but dual-key is also the narrower resale format, so that upside trades against exit liquidity rather than adding to it.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Do not use the 6.5% trailing URA 5yr CAGR: the backtest gives trailing CAGR ~zero forward power, momentum here is already negative (-0.684), and pooled project CAGR at Riversound is partly size-mix. The grounded numbers are realsmart's 4.8% realized annualized return over 275 profitable resales (avg 7.7yr holds, resale-to-resale) and the OCR forward baseline of +3.7%/yr. I use 4.0% as the working rate. Against that, a ~10% entry premium is ~3 years of return surrendered at purchase.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile for Riversound Residence - stack_profile status is not_researched, so no facing/stack join. Published unit mix (buycondo.sg) shows 1,475 sqft sits ambiguously across 4BR Compact (1163-1572), 4BR Utility (1292-1690), 4BR Dual Key (1421-1776) and even 3BR Dual Key (1184-1550) - and a live Riversound RENTAL listing advertises 1,475 sqft as '3 Bedrooms', consistent with a dual-key. The URA prints resolve what the brochure cannot: every 1450-1600 sqft sale ever recorded is floors 01-05 at a 9-13% floor-controlled discount to core stock, so whatever the type is called, the market prices it as the project's weak format. Running /research-development on Riversound would pin the stack and floor and is the cheapest way to firm this call up.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: realsmart resale-to-resale realized return (4.8%/yr over 275 profitable resales, avg 7.7yr holding) blended toward the backtested OCR forward baseline (+3.7%/yr); trailing 6.5% URA CAGR de-weighted per v3.4.1+ priors (no forward power, negative momentum, size-mix risk).
